title: Google Hardens Chrome Against ClickFix Attacks, Insecure HTTP Connections
description: Google has enhanced Chrome's security features to protect users against scams, social engineering, and insecure HTTP connections. New protections include two levels of Safe Browsing site warnings, server-side Gemini scam analysis, and detection of ClickFix attack commands. Chrome now warns users before connecting to unencrypted HTTP sites by default. These improvements aim to reduce phishing and social engineering risks, especially for users with Enhanced Protection enabled.
aiSummary: Google Chrome has introduced new security measures to defend against scams and social engineering attacks. These include a dual-level Safe Browsing warning system distinguishing between high-confidence malicious sites and suspicious sites using deceptive tactics. The Gemini scam detection engine has been moved server-side, expanding coverage to threats like fake antivirus and fake browser update pages. Chrome also detects ClickFix attacks, where users are tricked into running malicious commands, by analyzing clipboard content and warning users if dangerous commands are detected. Additionally, Chrome now prompts users for approval before connecting to HTTP sites, replacing the passive 'Not Secure' label with an active prompt to better protect user data. These features are integrated into Chrome's Enhanced Protection mode but are now enabled by default for all users.
aiImpact: These enhancements improve user protection against phishing, social engineering, and scams by providing more timely and accurate warnings about potentially malicious sites and commands. The HTTP connection prompt reduces the risk of data exposure over unencrypted connections. However, no direct vulnerability or exploit is described; rather, these are proactive security feature improvements to mitigate known attack techniques such as ClickFix and deceptive web content.
